## Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

This PR fixes an error I noticed while running `npm run test:e2e-setup` against my local instance as well as against a remote install. The specific issue I tripped over was that some `wp wc` CLI commands rejected the `--user` argument when it was placed after the `wc` token in the command. This PR ensures that we always use `wp --user={USER_ARG} wc ...` to ensure that the user argument is processed by the main `wp` command.

Here are examples:
```
wp wc --user=demo tool run install_pages
Error: Parameter errors:
 unknown --user parameter

wp wc shipping_zone create --name="Everywhere" --order=1 --user=demo
Error: Parameter errors:
 unknown --user parameter

wp wc shipping_zone_method create 1 --method_id="flat_rate" --user=demo
Error: Parameter errors:
 unknown --user parameter
```

These issues seem to occur with newer versions of PHP 8.x, so I have seen them mostly for Jurassic.ninja sites.

This pull request provides a fix to request stream usage across all assigned partition consumers, i.e. ingest-limits pods. Querying stream usage was broken accidentally when the query-only-owning-instances optimizations was introduced by:
- #16937 

The purpose of the aforementioned optimization was to eliminate unnecessary query of ingest limits instances. However following this approach breaks the general service goal to provide an accurate global max active stream counter per tenant.

## Summary When using Puppeteer's `Page.screenshot` for capturing screenshots, viewport changes can occur, resulting in a visual effect where the page briefly flickers: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1257fe6d-098f-4536-a947-b4579830d873 After reviewing [GitHub Issue #7043](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/issues/7043), it was found that setting `captureBeyondViewport: false` did not resolve the issue. Further investigation into [StackOverflow: puppeteer-page-screenshot-resizes-viewport](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68059664/puppeteer-page-screenshot-resizes-viewport) revealed that setting `defaultViewport: null` effectively addresses the problem. However, we have specific requirements to set `width` and `height`, so this approach is not ideal for our use case. Based on our analysis, the root cause seems to be related to `defaultViewport.deviceScaleFactor`. When left at its default value of `1`, it can lead to inconsistencies in `deviceScaleFactor`, indirectly causing the screenshot flickering issue. Referring to the [Puppeteer viewport API documentation](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.viewport), we discovered that setting `deviceScaleFactor` to `0` resets it to the system default. Testing this approach confirmed that it effectively resolves the problem. > [CDP API: Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Emulation/#method-setDeviceMetricsOverride)
### Final Solution: Set `defaultViewport.deviceScaleFactor` to `0` and `captureBeyondViewport` to `false`. This combination eliminates the viewport flickering issue during screenshot operations. ## Checklist - [ ] Added or updated necessary tests (Optional). - [x] Updated documentation to align with changes (Optional). - [x] Verified no breaking changes, or prepared solutions for any occurring breaking changes (Optional). - [x] My change does not involve the above items.

## Why I'm doing:
When https://github.com/StarRocks/starrocks/pull/56932 is merged, mv rewrite may generate bad plans for query with left joins, plan may loss partition predicates in some cases.

The root cause is `RuleSet.PARTITION_PRUNE_RULES` cannot be redo even if mv rewrite has failed.

## What I'm doing:

`RuleSet.PARTITION_PRUNE_RULES` should be used very carefully, since it contains bitset to mark whether it has been applied, so this action will prevent partition pruning later. reset partition prune bit to do partition prune again because:
 1. partition prune is not done well since some predicates have not been pushed down.
 2. it may generate bad plans if we do not do partition prune again.

This pull request fixes the linear_delete_issue function to correctly delete a single issue in Linear.

Currently, when executing linear_delete_issue, the following error is raised:
```
Failed to delete issue: GraphQL operation failed: Unknown argument "ids" on field "Mutation.issueDelete". Did you mean "id"?
```
This indicates that the GraphQL mutation incorrectly uses ids (plural) instead of the expected id (singular).

## Changes
- Added a new mutation DELETE_ISSUE_MUTATION that correctly accepts a single id.
- Updated LinearGraphQLClient.deleteIssue to use DELETE_ISSUE_MUTATION instead of DELETE_ISSUES_MUTATION.
- Added a unit test to verify that a single issue can be deleted properly.

# 設定ファイルの更新

## 概要
TypeScriptプロジェクトの設定ファイル（`package.json`と`tsconfig.json`）を更新し、より適切な開発環境を構築します。

## 変更内容

### package.json の更新
- スクリプトコマンドのパスを修正（`supabase/scripts/`を追加）
- 新しいスクリプトを追加：
  - `clear:storage`: ストレージバケットのクリア
  - `move:images`: 画像ファイルの移動とリネーム
  - `type-check`: TypeScriptの型チェック
  - `build`: TypeScriptのビルド
- 不要な`type: "commonjs"`設定を削除

### tsconfig.json の更新
- プロジェクトのルート設定を追加：
  - `rootDir`と`baseUrl`を設定
  - パスエイリアス（`@/*`）を追加
- コンパイル対象の調整：
  - `supabase/scripts/**/*`を追加
  - `types/**/*`を追加
  - `dist`をexcludeに追加

## 動作確認項目
- [ ] 各npmスクリプトが正常に実行できること
- [ ] TypeScriptの型チェックが正常に動作すること
- [ ] パスエイリアスが正常に解決されること
